title: Change Safety Conductor & Stateful Recovery Playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a Change Safety Conductor that performs safe config applies for batching and caching knobs, runs dry-run cost/latency simulations, executes canary/shadow applies, and performs automated stateful rollback and reconciliation when guardrails are violated. This ticket covers the orchestration, decision scoring, state checkpoints, and remediation playbook for config changes that materially affect token cost, KV cache behavior, or batching heuristics.
background: We frequently need to ship configuration changes (batch_size, batch_window_ms, kv_cache_enable, cache_eviction_strategy, quantization_profile) that can have outsized impact on inference unit economics and latency SLOs. Past incidents show manual rollbacks are slow or incomplete due to distributed state (cache shards, ongoing KV sessions, dynamic batching warm-up). We need an automated conductor that: 1) predicts cost/latency delta from proposed changes, 2) executes safe canary/shadow applies, 3) detects regressions, and 4) performs deterministic stateful rollback + reconciliation with operator oversight.
progress_updates: 2026-03-06: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra, and console teams. Agreed on core goals and SLOs.
2026-03-08: Prototype of dry-run simulator that replays short traffic traces through batching/kvsim; initial cost delta predictions within 10% of observed in staging.
2026-03-10: Security & compliance flagged audit log requirements and KMS markers for any automated rollback action.
2026-03-12: Implemented checkpoint store schema in internal config-change-history service and added deterministic op IDs for apply/rollback flows.
2026-03-14: Integration test failing on shard reconciliation timeout; added exponential backoff + compensating cache flush task.
design_notes: Conductor is a distributed coordinator that sequences these phases: 1) Validation (schema + preflight rules), 2) Simulation (cost/latency estimator using sampled traces + model perf profiles), 3) Canary Apply (shadow traffic or small shard rollouts), 4) Monitoring & Scoring (SLO regressions, cost delta, error rates), 5a) Promote to Global or 5b) Rollback (or staged remediation). Key primitives: atomic config transaction with checkpoint, idempotent rollback handlers, reconciliation loop comparing desired vs observed state, TTL-based hysteresis to avoid flapping, and operator override APIs. We store per-change checkpoints (serialized flat metadata) and a timeline of observed metrics for audit and diagnosis.
tradeoffs: Conductor centralization vs per-cluster autonomy: central coordinator simplifies policy but adds single-point-of-failure; mitigation: HA leader election and local fallback agents.
Simulation fidelity vs speed: high-fidelity sim needs longer traces and model evals (slow); choose fast estimator for preflight and targeted high-fidelity sim only for high-risk changes.
Automated rollback aggressiveness: aggressive rollbacks reduce BLAST radius but increase flapping risk; implement hysteresis windows and require multi-metric confirmation before automatic rollback.
Stateful rollback complexity: fully idempotent state restoration (eg cache warmup) is costly; instead implement compensation actions (warm-up jobs, cache TTL re-seed) post-rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor can run a preflight simulation and output a cost/latency delta estimate in <30s for typical config change.
Canary apply path can perform a 5% traffic canary with automatic health checks and promote/rollback decision in <10 minutes.
Automated rollback triggers on any of: latency P99 increase > 25% sustained over 2 minutes, cost-per-token increase > 20% projected and observed, or error-rate uplift > 3x baseline.
All automated actions are recorded in audit logs with KMS-signed operation IDs and a link to the checkpoint artifact.
Reconciliation loop detects drift between desired and observed config within 90s and converges back to desired state or documents failure with remediation steps.
E2E tests in CI simulate a change that requires rollback and assert stateful recovery path completes and caches are in consistent state.
Documentation and runbook published and reviewed by SRE and PM; demo performed with stakeholders.
tasks: Design API for Conductor: POST /changesets -> returns op_id + preflight report
Implement preflight cost/latency estimator service and integrate sampled traces
Create checkpoint storage schema and lifecycle (retention, encryption)
Build canary apply agent with shadow traffic support and small-shard rollout logic
Implement automated scoring rules and pluggable metrics: latency, error-rate, cost, quality (evals)
Implement rollback handlers per subsystem: serving runtime, cache shards, autoscaler policies
Implement reconciliation loop with exponential backoff and operator alerts
Add CI integration tests and chaos scenarios for partial failures

tests: Unit tests for estimator (cost delta prediction) with synthetic workloads
Integration test: end-to-end canary apply and automatic promote/rollback based on simulated metric stream
Chaos test: simulate partial failure of checkpoint store and verify safe abort
Reconciliation test: verify convergence after transient network partition
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal-only with dry-run and read-only preflight reports. Phase 1: enable canary apply for non-customer-impacting configs (batching heuristics) in staging. Phase 2: limited production rollout behind feature flag for beta customers with operator approvals. Phase 3: full automation for low-risk classes with auto-rollback enabled; gradual ramp and close monitoring for two weeks.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Conductor itself causes outages if buggy. Mitigation: default to safe-readonly mode and require two-person approval for initial production enables.
Risk: Over-aggressive rollbacks lead to oscillation. Mitigation: implement hysteresis windows + cooldown periods + rate limits on automated rollback frequency.
Risk: Checkpoint store corruption. Mitigation: immutable, versioned checkpoints with quorum replication and smoke-validation on restore.
Risk: Cost estimator blindspots for new models. Mitigation: conservative uncertainty multiplier and mandatory manual review for changes affecting new model types.
approvals: Lina Hsu (SRE) - Approved provisional rollout plan
notes_for_reviewers: Reviewers: focus on the rollback decision matrix (scoring thresholds) and the reconciliation convergence guarantees. Pay special attention to required observability signals (per-shard P99, per-model token-cost) and how they map to trigger rules. Expect follow-ups to tune thresholds after initial beta.
next_steps: 1) Finalize scoring thresholds and map to alerting dashboards. 2) Complete PR for estimator and checkpoint store. 3) Schedule SRE drill for week of 2026-03-22. 4) Start Phase 0 internal dry-run by 2026-03-20.
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids hard-coding rollback thresholds in code; thresholds live in Config Policy service so PM and SRE can iterate without deploys. All ops are surfaced in Console with links to checkpoints and the CI test that validated the change.
